chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Refining the act and the song Rhythm For Sale
summary: Nazarro and Bubbles reshaped their routines; Green recites the lyrics of Rhythm For Sale, Buck and Bubbles' theme written by a freelance composer.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So, as you began to perform more and more, you began to refine your act.
What sort of things did you cut away from it? What sort of mistakes were you making?

Well, we weren't actually making mistakes. The idea was they loved improvement, you see, and it was either Nat Nazarra or John Bubbles thought that it would be better for us, it would be more of an improvement for to improve on there to take that away and don't do it first, do it second, and like that, whatever they had us doing. So --
Were there things that you created on your own?

Well, we had our dance, like 'Sweet Sue', and 'Broadway Melody', and 'Bugle Call Rag', you know, like those things. One time Daddy had us to doing like 'Broadway Melody', and then Buck and Bubbles' theme song, which was, 'Rhythm For Sale'. And eventually, see, they taught us how to sing the song, see, and M.C. Bubbles had sung it, and Buck and Bubbles were both of them singing it first. After they got on the stage they would sing. Bubbles would sing the verse to 'Rhythm For Sale', and then Mr. Buck was playing the piano and he joined in singing the chorus with him, and they'd sing it, you see, and people enjoyed 'Rhythm For Sale'. It was a nice melody song, you see.
Well, it's -- I can talk it over for you, because I'm not in too great a voice today, but I can give
you an idea how it goes. It says --
Was there tap dancing with it as well?

Yeah. Well, that's where we came in, see, because we were tap dancing "Sweet Sue". That was a melody. "Rhythm For Sale" was a special song written for Buck and Bubbles. It was a theme, like to come on stage, see?

Some fellow there. He was a freelance composer, you know. Forget his name. Nice guy, person. Well, anyhow, he specialized in that. You had a lot of music writers around Broadway then that was trying to get recognition, and he happened to be one, you know. Nazarré, Nat Nazarré knew him, you see. He got him to write this song, see. I'll explain it by words where it says. The verse of the song says, "Years ago, a certain sage said the whole world was a stage, and the colored people were the players from the start. If it's so that the colored folks, with their songs and dance and jokes, in a show must play a special part." Then it said, "Without a doubt." Then the melody begins. "All the world is rhythm mad, all the world wants rhythm bad. Colored folks are mighty glad, because they've got rhythm for sale. Everybody on this earth is in search of joy and mirth. Colored folks is rich from birth because they've got rhythm for sale. Up in Harlem they are doing swell. Nature gave them
something they can sell. Everybody on this earth is in search of joy and mirth. Colored folks are rich from birth because they've got rhythm for sale."

Yeah. That's Buck and Bubbles' theme song. So they -- eventually they taught us to sing the song and then do the "Sweet Sue" tap dance to "Rhythm For Sale". They was trying to popularize the song, you see, and that's what we did.
